method: The finished size is the sewn-in size of one short side of the half-square triangle, measured without seam allowances. An exact cut needs the allowance on all three sides, so the finished size grows by the allowance times (2 + sqrt(2)): one allowance for each leg plus the allowance along the 45 degree hypotenuse. Two at a time uses a starting square of that value; four at a time, where the square is sewn around the perimeter and cut on both diagonals, uses the value times sqrt(2); eight at a time, where the square is also cut on both midlines, uses the value times 2. Two starting squares are paired for every batch, yielding 2, 4 or 8 units. The cutting size is rounded up to the next 1/8 inch, or to the next whole millimetre in metric mode, and the exact minimum is shown beside it. The trim size is the finished size plus twice the allowance, the size an unfinished unit measures after pressing. Batches are the number of units needed divided by the yield and rounded up, so whole pairs can leave spare units. Ranges are 0.25 to 60 inches (0.635 to 152.4 centimetres) for the finished size, 0.1 to 1 inch (0.254 to 2.54 centimetres) for the seam allowance and 1 to 2000 for the quantity; a non-numeric, out-of-range or fractional quantity, an unknown unit or method, and a missing field are rejected with an action message. Conversions use exactly 2.54 centimetres per inch. The figures assume straight-grain squares and a seam allowance held exactly: fabric stretch, a scant seam, pressing distortion, directional prints and trimming to square up are not modelled, and the tool adds no trimming room. The calculation runs entirely in the browser with no storage, uploads or network access.

sources.title: Quilting convention: a finished half-square triangle is the sewn-in size of one short side, and the unfinished unit is that size plus a seam allowance on both legs
Half-square triangle cutting rules: finished size plus 7/8 inch for two at a time, and perimeter-sewn squares scaled by the square root of two for four at a time and by two for eight at a time
